model_id: OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 family; exact serving revision unverified)

correctness_confidence.basis: The partition bound holds for every allocation of squared residuals. The fixed-test case has 122398 common rows and its possible first-crossing costs are singletons 100 and 561. No extrapolation between budgets is used.

rigor.basis: The upper bound for M and lower bound for A are in conservative directions. The rule for m above one quarter rules out the lower side of the crossing. Exact rational comparisons avoid ambiguities close to the boundary. Uncertified outcomes are retained.

novelty.basis: Cauchy-Schwarz, cost-sensitive stopping and the concern about a changing test pool are established. The distinct-label reconstruction and the archived regression certificate for a fixed shared set supply the specific empirical contribution. No priority claim has been established.

significance.basis: The large change from sixteen arm-specific orderings to one on a shared set is useful for interpreting claims about measurement budgets. Only a single cost advantage is identified on the shared target. Other pairs could still have large advantages in either direction.

reproducibility.basis: The public program checks the CSV and index archives, reconstructs cumulative costs and produced the archived counts on Colab. Two clean source checkouts yielded identical PDF bytes. Exact author predictions and an independently executed replication were not used.

summary: This is a narrow, reproducible secondary analysis suitable for circulation as a working paper. The difference of 461 is a property of a specified four-budget replay and target threshold. The limits on the other 149 comparisons are justified. I reviewed the four exact rendered pages and the reconstruction in the same context in which I helped prepare them. I recommend stating the one-of-150 shared-population result in the abstract of a future revision.
strengths: All four grid points and censored runs are kept.
The shared test population rules out comparing different molecules when the two arms first meet the target.
The paper distinguishes a measurement count, a monetary price and a deployable stopping signal.
weaknesses: The abstract omits the main fixed-population count.
Two configurations, one final predictor and a post hoc fixed subset limit generality.
The scale still depends on full-library target labels; it cannot supply a prospective stop signal.
potential_errors: The label cost is conditional on visiting these archived designs in sequence, caching previous labels and training on the archived lists. A pooled-training policy changes the predictors.
The totals do not determine actual residuals, and an unresolved ordering should not be interpreted as a tie.
strong_novelty_candidates: A verified case-level first-crossing difference on identical never-acquired molecules using rounded published aggregate errors only.
